claims.statement: Each workspace runs jest suites (unit tests plus e2e-specs against throwaway stores), and every service ships a health.e2e-spec.ts asserting the shared kernel health dialect — identical across services as deliberate conformance duplication.

The Playwright harness uses slot-owned infrastructure: ports derived as basePort + 10*slot (31xx production stack, 32xx dev stack, 33xx hop tests), per-slot containers redis-e2e-<slot>, feedback-pg-e2e-<slot>, rabbitmq-e2e-<slot>, and a per-worktree queue so concurrent worktrees never collide.

Explicit env overrides (E2E_*_PORT, TEST_REDIS_URL) always win over the slot-derived values, and the production-build and next-dev stacks run in separate Playwright invocations because they share apps/app/.next.

scripts/coverage.mjs merges every jest and node --test suite's lcov into one repository-relative .coverage/lcov.info, rewriting SF: paths and keeping the most-covered run's hit counts for doubly-instrumented files.
Contract tripwires are real tests: UI token values live in packages/ui/test/tokens.test.ts and arch-check's rules are covered by scripts/arch-check.test.mjs under node --test.

The arch-check suite proves its rules can fail: tests plant a violation (shared store, missing env forwarding, a self-hosted runner in a workflow) and assert the finding, and assert today's tree is clean.
Cached-row discipline is asserted structurally (exact cached key list, enc.v1. on the payload, decrypt-and-compare), not by literal string search in ciphertext.
